value_domain: Dollar amount claimed for advertising for tenants
value_source: ATO, Rental properties guide 2025, Rental expenses
variable_description: What the owner spent advertising the property to find tenants, deducted in full in the year it was incurred. The ATO lists "advertising for tenants" among the expenses for which "You may be able to claim an immediate deduction in the income year you incur the expense". Advertising to sell is a different thing entirely, and is not in this column: the guide puts "advertising expenses" among acquisition and disposal costs, which are not deductible.
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction claimed for the year, at the owner's share of the property rather than the full outlay where the property is co-owned.
limitation: It is not a signal that the property was vacant, because agents advertise between tenancies and for rent reviews alike, and a property let through the same tenant for years can still carry a fee. Nor can it be read as marketing for sale, since selling costs are excluded from the schedule and go to the cost base instead.
rationale: The rental properties guide lists advertising for tenants as an immediately deductible rental expense and separately excludes advertising to sell as a disposal cost, which is the distinction this column needs.
evidence_quote: You can't claim a deduction for the costs of acquiring or disposing of your rental property
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that letting advertising is deductible here while selling advertising is excluded from the schedule.

value_domain: Dollar amount claimed for body corporate fees and charges
value_source: ATO, Rental properties guide 2025, Rental expenses
variable_description: Strata levies the owner paid for the day-to-day running of the building, claimed in the year they were incurred. The ATO treats ordinary levies as payment for services: "Regular payments you make to body corporate administration funds or general purpose sinking funds for ongoing administration and general maintenance are considered to be payments for the provision of services by the body corporate." Special levies for capital improvements are excluded, and become capital works deductions once the work is finished.
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for regular administration and general purpose sinking fund contributions, at the owner's share, excluding special capital levies.
limitation: The figure bundles costs the other columns name separately, so adding it to gardening, insurance or repairs double counts: the ATO warns "you can't claim a separate deduction for common garden maintenance if that expense is already included in body corporate fees and charges". A strata property with high levies and empty maintenance columns is therefore not a cheaper property to run.
rationale: The rental properties guide defines what body corporate fees cover, which levies are excluded and which expenses must not be claimed twice alongside them.
evidence_quote: For example, you can't claim a separate deduction for common garden maintenance if that expense is already included in body corporate fees and charges.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the levy bundles services other columns also name, or that special capital levies are excluded.

value_domain: Dollar amount claimed for borrowing expenses
value_source: ATO, Rental properties guide 2025, Rental expenses
variable_description: This year's slice of the costs of setting up the loan, written off over five years rather than deducted at once. The ATO defines the spread: "If your total borrowing expenses are more than $100, the deduction is spread over 5 years (starting from the day when the loan is taken out) or the term of the loan, whichever is less." The costs themselves are loan establishment and title search fees, mortgage document and broker fees, mortgage stamp duty, lender-required valuations and lender's mortgage insurance.
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for the year, being an apportioned share of the total borrowing costs, or the whole amount where those costs were $100 or less.
limitation: It is not cash the owner spent this year. An amount here can come from a loan taken out four years ago, and the year a loan is repaid early carries the whole unclaimed balance at once, which looks like a spike in costs when nothing was bought. Interest and the stamp duty on the property transfer are excluded, so it is not the cost of borrowing in any economic sense.
rationale: The rental properties guide lists what counts as a borrowing expense, what does not, and the five-year spreading rule that decides how much appears in a given year.
evidence_quote: If your total borrowing expenses are more than $100, the deduction is spread over 5 years (starting from the day when the loan is taken out) or the term of the loan, whichever is less.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount is an apportioned write-off of loan set-up costs rather than spending in the year.

value_domain: Dollar amount claimed for decline in value of depreciating assets
value_source: ATO, Rental properties guide 2025, Rental expenses
variable_description: The write-down of the plant inside the property - stoves, air conditioners, carpets and the like - claimed for the year. The ATO puts it among the deductions spread over several years, letting an owner "claim a deduction for the decline in value of certain capital (depreciating) assets", worked out "using either the diminishing value method or the prime cost method" and reduced for any use that is not for a taxable purpose. Fixtures that form part of the building are not here: they are construction expenditure and belong in the capital works column instead.
value_definition: A whole-dollar non-cash deduction for the year, at the owner's share, covering assets treated as plant rather than as part of the building.
limitation: The series breaks in 2017. From 1 July 2017 most second-hand depreciating assets in a residential rental can no longer be claimed, so a fall in this column after that date reflects the law rather than the condition of the property, and comparisons across the change are not like for like. The amount is also an accounting write-down, so it never corresponds to money spent in the year.
rationale: The rental properties guide defines the deduction, separates plant from construction expenditure and states the second-hand asset limit that changes the column's meaning from 1 July 2017.
evidence_quote: From 1 July 2017, reduce your deduction by the extent you installed or used the asset in your residential rental property to derive rental income and the asset was a second-hand depreciating asset (unless an exception applies).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount is a non-cash write-down or that the second-hand asset rules changed it in 2017.

value_domain: Dollar amount claimed for cleaning
value_source: ATO, Rental properties guide 2025, Rental expenses
variable_description: What the owner paid to have the property cleaned while it was rented or genuinely available for rent. Cleaning is on the ATO's list of expenses for which an immediate deduction is available in the year incurred, and the guide's own worked example puts it among the ordinary running costs of a let property. It is claimed only for the letting period, since deductions run "for the period you rent your property or it's genuinely available for rent".
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for the year at the owner's share, covering cleaning services the owner actually paid for.
limitation: A nil value is weak evidence of anything: a strata owner's cleaning may already sit inside the body corporate fees column, a tenant may have paid it, and the ATO allows a deduction "only if you actually incur them and they are not paid by the tenant". An initial clean before first letting is also treated as capital and does not appear.
rationale: The rental properties guide lists cleaning as an immediately deductible rental expense and states both the letting-period condition and the requirement that the owner actually incurred the cost.
evidence_quote: You can claim a deduction for these expenses only if you actually incur them and they are not paid by the tenant.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the claim depends on the owner incurring the cost during the letting period.

value_domain: Dollar amount claimed for council rates
value_source: ATO, Rental properties guide 2025, Rental expenses
variable_description: Local council rates on the rental property, claimed for the part of the year it was rented or genuinely available for rent. The ATO lists local council rates among the immediately deductible expenses, and allows them during renovation of a property the owner intends to rent: "You can claim expenditure such as interest on loans, local council, water and sewerage rates, land taxes and emergency service levies you incur during renovations to a property you intend to rent out." Rates on genuinely vacant land are generally excluded.
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for the year at the owner's share, apportioned to the period of rental use where the property was not let for the whole year.
limitation: It is not the rates bill. A holiday home let for part of the year carries only the apportioned share, a co-owner carries a fraction, and vacant land holding costs are denied outright, so the column understates what the council charged. It also cannot be used to value the property, since rating bases and revaluation cycles differ by council.
rationale: The rental properties guide lists council rates as an immediately deductible expense, describes the apportionment to the rental period and sets out the vacant land denial that removes some rates from the claim.
evidence_quote: You can claim expenditure such as interest on loans, local council, water and sewerage rates, land taxes and emergency service levies you incur during renovations to a property you intend to rent out.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount is apportioned to the letting period and to the owner's share rather than being the rates assessed.

value_domain: Dollar amount claimed for capital works deductions
value_source: ATO, Rental properties guide 2025, Rental expenses
variable_description: The year's write-off of building and structural work, spread across decades rather than deducted when it was built. The ATO explains that "You can deduct certain kinds of construction expenditure. In the case of residential rental properties, the deductions would generally be spread over a period of 25 or 40 years", with no deduction until construction is complete. Extensions, alterations and structural improvements qualify; repairs and plant do not, and belong in their own columns.
value_definition: A whole-dollar non-cash deduction for the year, capped in total by the original construction expenditure and available only for the days the property was rented or genuinely available for rent.
limitation: A value here says construction happened at some point, not that any money was spent this year, and the eligible rate depends on when construction started rather than on what the work cost. The claim also reaches forward to the sale: expenditure deducted as capital works cannot be counted again in the cost base, so a large figure here raises the eventual capital gain.
rationale: The rental properties guide defines capital works deductions, the periods over which they are spread, what construction qualifies and the interaction with the cost base.
evidence_quote: You can deduct certain kinds of construction expenditure. In the case of residential rental properties, the deductions would generally be spread over a period of 25 or 40 years.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the deduction is a long-run write-off of construction rather than spending in the year.

value_domain: Dollar amount claimed for gardening and lawn mowing
value_source: ATO, Rental properties guide 2025, Rental expenses
variable_description: What the owner paid for gardening and lawn mowing at the rental property during the letting period. The ATO lists "gardening and lawn mowing" among the expenses immediately deductible in the year they are incurred, and it appears as its own line in the guide's net rental income worksheet. Work that goes beyond upkeep, such as landscaping a new garden, is capital and is not claimed here.
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for the year at the owner's share, covering routine grounds maintenance the owner paid for.
limitation: It is not a measure of how much grounds a property has. Strata owners usually have common garden maintenance inside their body corporate levy and cannot claim it again here, tenants often mow their own lawns, and landscaping is capitalised, so an empty column is common for properties with substantial gardens.
rationale: The rental properties guide lists gardening and lawn mowing as an immediately deductible expense and names it as a separate line of the net rental income worksheet.
evidence_quote: gardening and lawn mowing
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said why the column is often empty for properties that plainly have gardens.

value_domain: Dollar amount claimed for insurance premiums
value_source: ATO, Rental properties guide 2025, Rental expenses
variable_description: Premiums the owner paid to insure the rental property and the income it produces. The guide's immediate deduction list breaks the cover into four kinds - building, contents, public liability and loss of rent - so a single figure here can be any mix of them. What the insurer pays out does not net off against it: "If you receive an insurance or compensation payment for work you paid for and claimed as a deduction in an earlier year, you need to include it in your income."
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for the year at the owner's share, covering building, contents, public liability and loss of rent premiums.
limitation: It is gross of any recovery, so a year with a large claim shows a premium here and a receipt in the income columns rather than a reduced cost. Building insurance carried inside a strata levy also cannot be claimed again, so strata properties look underinsured on this measure, and premiums on policies that protect the owner's loan rather than the property are outside it.
rationale: The rental properties guide lists the insurance types that are immediately deductible and states how an insurance recovery is treated, which is what stops the column being read as a net cost.
evidence_quote: You can't claim a deduction for repairs if your insurer pays for the work. If you receive an insurance or compensation payment for work you paid for and claimed as a deduction in an earlier year, you need to include it in your income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said which covers the premium can include, or that payouts appear as income rather than as an offset here.

value_domain: Dollar amount claimed for land tax
value_source: ATO, Rental properties guide 2025, Rental expenses
variable_description: State land tax on the rental property, claimed in the year the liability arose rather than the year it was paid. The ATO is explicit about arrears: "When you receive land tax assessments in arrears, the amount of land tax isn't deductible in the income year in which you pay the arrears. The land tax amounts are deductible in the respective income years to which the liability for the land tax relates." The timing of the liability itself is set by each state's own law.
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for the year the liability relates to, at the owner's share, sourced from state and territory land tax rather than any Commonwealth tax.
limitation: A zero usually means the owner sat under a state threshold, not that the property was exempt from tax, so the column measures a threshold crossing as much as a tax burden. Amounts are also not comparable between states, since rates, thresholds and aggregation rules differ, and an owner with several properties is assessed on their combined holding rather than on this one.
rationale: The rental properties guide states when land tax is deductible, how arrears are attributed to the years the liability relates to, and that the timing depends on state legislation.
evidence_quote: When you receive land tax assessments in arrears, the amount of land tax isn't deductible in the income year in which you pay the arrears. The land tax amounts are deductible in the respective income years to which the liability for the land tax relates.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount is attributed to the year the liability arose and depends on state thresholds.

value_domain: Dollar total of the rental expense columns
value_source: ATO, Rental properties guide 2025, Worksheet - work out your net rental income or loss
variable_description: The sum of every rental expense claimed for the property, and the figure taken off gross rent to get net rent. The ATO's worksheet lays the arithmetic out directly, running from the individual expense lines to a "Total expenses" line and then to "Net rental income or loss" as gross rent minus that total. It is the single number that decides whether the property was negatively geared for this owner in this year.
value_definition: A whole-dollar total at the owner's share, adding the immediate deductions to the borrowing, decline in value and capital works write-offs on the same row.
limitation: Adding it to the expense columns beside it counts everything twice, because it is their subtotal rather than another cost. It is also not the cost of running the property: it is one owner's share, it includes non-cash write-downs, and it excludes anything the tenant paid or the law denied, such as travel to inspect a residential rental.
rationale: The ATO worksheet shows the total expenses line as the sum of the individual expense items and shows net rental income or loss being calculated from it, which is exactly how the schedule row is built.
evidence_quote: Net rental income or loss ($9,300 minus $20,629) −$11,329
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount is the subtotal of the other expense columns on the same row.

value_domain: Date the property first produced rental income
value_source: ATO, Rental properties guide 2025, Rental expenses
variable_description: The day the property first earned rent for this owner, which fixes how long it has been an investment. It matters because deductions run from availability rather than ownership: the ATO allows a deduction "for certain expenses you incur for the period you rent your property or it's genuinely available for rent". Read with the income year on the same row, it gives the number of years the property has been let, which is the closest thing in the schedule to a holding period.
value_definition: A calendar date, constant for a property across the owner's schedule rows in later years, and earlier than or equal to the income year on the row.
limitation: It is neither the purchase date nor the date the property became available for rent, so it cannot date acquisition or measure a vacancy before first letting. A property bought, renovated and advertised over eighteen months carries expenses in years before this date, and a home that was lived in first will show a date long after purchase.
rationale: The rental properties guide sets the availability test that decides when rental deductions begin, which is what makes the date of first rental income the reference point for a property's letting history.
evidence_quote: You can claim a deduction for certain expenses you incur for the period you rent your property or it's genuinely available for rent.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the date marks first rent rather than purchase or first availability.

value_domain: Australian financial year of the rental schedule extract
value_source: ATO, Rental properties guide 2025, Rental income
variable_description: The financial year of the rental schedule file this row belongs to, constant within a table. The schedule is annual and reports one property for one owner, so the year is what separates a landlord's 2015-16 row for a flat from the 2016-17 row for the same flat. Reference periods matter here because rent and every expense on the row are twelve-month totals: nothing on the schedule is a point-in-time figure.
value_definition: A financial year label rather than a date, one value per table, matching the year in the table name.
limitation: It does not say the property was let for the whole year. A schedule exists for any year the property earned rent or was available for rent, so a row can cover a fortnight, and the weeks-rented column rather than this one carries that fact.
rationale: The column is constant within each rental schedule table and matches the table name, and the ATO guide describes the schedule quantities as annual totals of rent and expenses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the value is constant within a table or that the amounts beside it are annual totals.

value_domain: Financial year the rental schedule reports (income year)
value_source: ATO, Foreign income return form guide, glossary entry Income year
variable_description: The income year the rent and expenses on this row belong to, running 1 July to 30 June. The ATO's definition leaves room for exceptions: an income year "is, in effect, a 12-month period ending on 30 June, or a 12-month period ending on another date where the Commissioner has approved that other date under section 18 of the Act". The rental figures are reported at question 21 of the supplementary return for that year, so this column is what ties the schedule to the return.
value_definition: A year identifier for a 1 July to 30 June period, usually held as the ending year or as a paired label such as 2014-15.
limitation: It is not the year the return was lodged or amended, so a late lodgment or a revised claim still carries the year the rent was earned. Land tax on the same row can also relate to a different year again, because arrears are deductible in the years the liability arose rather than the year of payment.
rationale: The ATO glossary gives the statutory meaning of an income year, and the return instructions show rental income and deductions being reported for that year at question 21.
evidence_quote: An income year - or year of income - is, in effect, a 12-month period ending on 30 June, or a 12-month period ending on another date where the Commissioner has approved that other date under section 18 of the Act.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the year is the year the rent was earned rather than the year the schedule was lodged.

value_domain: Local government area, ASGS 2023 non-ABS structure
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Local Government Areas
variable_description: The council area the rental property sits in, coded to the 2023 release of ABS local government areas. It describes the property, not the landlord, so an owner living in one city and letting in another is placed here by the asset rather than by their home address. The 2023 boundaries are also the 2024 boundaries: the ABS records that "The 2024 release of Local Government Areas is unchanged from the 2023 Local Government Areas release."
value_definition: A five-digit code, a one-digit state or territory identifier followed by a four-digit council identifier, approximated from whole mesh blocks in the 2023 release of the classification.
limitation: One boundary vintage is applied to every year this column covers, so a property in a council that was amalgamated appears in the merged council even in years before the merger, and council-level counts over time are not what the councils of the day would have reported. The ABS also warns these approximations "should only be used for statistical purposes", so they cannot be used to attribute rates or council policy.
rationale: The ABS standard defines local government areas as a mesh block approximation, sets out the five-digit coding and states that the 2024 release is unchanged from the 2023 release this column is coded to.
evidence_quote: The 2024 release of Local Government Areas is unchanged from the 2023 Local Government Areas release.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the code locates the rental property rather than the owner, or which release of the boundaries it uses.

value_domain: ABS Local Government Area code, ASGS Edition 3 (2024)
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Non ABS Structures: Local Government Areas
variable_description: The council area the rental property sits in, coded to the ABS Local Government Area list rather than to the council's own boundary. The ABS says its areas "are an ABS Mesh Block approximation of gazetted local government boundaries as defined by each state and territory" and warns that they "do not match official legal boundaries and should only be used for statistical purposes". Because the whole schedule is a per-property record, this is the property's council, not the landlord's, and one owner with three properties has three rows with three different codes.
value_definition: A five-digit ABS Local Government Area code, made up of a one-digit state or territory identifier and a four-digit area identifier. The ASGS Edition 3 page reports 567 Local Government Areas covering the whole of Australia, including unincorporated areas, with 19 non-spatial special purpose codes, but the ABS reviews the list every year, so the 2024 vintage this column carries may not hold exactly that count.
limitation: It cannot be used as a legal statement of which council governs the property, since the boundary is a mesh block approximation. One vintage of the list is applied to every income year in the file, so a code cannot be read as the council area in force at the time and rate or land-tax settings of that year cannot be attached to it safely.
rationale: The column is an ABS LGA code on a row whose other geography columns (mesh block, SA1 to SA4, state) are the same property geocoded at different levels, and the ABS page defines how LGAs are built and what they can be used for.
evidence_quote: Local Government Areas are an ABS Mesh Block approximation of gazetted local government boundaries as defined by each state and territory.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Local Government Area' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so it never said whose area it is or that the boundary is an approximation.

value_domain: Dollar amount claimed at the legal expenses line of the rental property schedule
value_source: ATO, Rental properties guide 2025, Rental expenses
variable_description: Legal costs the owner claimed as a deduction against this property's rent for the year. The ATO allows only revenue legal costs here - "evicting a non-paying tenant", "taking court action for loss of rental income" and "defending damages claims for injuries suffered by a third party on your rental property" - and says "Most legal expenses, however, are of a capital nature and are therefore not deductible". So a non-zero value is usually a sign of a tenancy dispute rather than of conveyancing.
value_definition: A dollar amount, one of the named expense lines that add to EXPNSS_TOTL_AMT on the same row and are subtracted from RNTL_GRS_AMT to give RNTL_NET_RNT_AMT.
limitation: It records a claim, not an adjudicated deduction, so a conveyancing or title-defence cost that should have gone to the property's cost base can still appear here. A zero is not evidence of no legal spending: the capital legal costs of buying and selling never reach the schedule at all.
rationale: The guide's legal expenses section lists exactly which legal costs belong at this line of the rental worksheet and which are capital, which is the distinction a reader needs before treating the column as legal spending.
evidence_quote: Most legal expenses, however, are of a capital nature and are therefore not deductible.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label 'Legal Fees' as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said that most legal costs on a rental property are excluded from it.

value_domain: Dollar amount claimed at the interest on loans line of the rental property schedule
value_source: ATO, Rental properties guide 2025, Rental expenses, Interest on loans
variable_description: Interest the owner claimed on money borrowed for this property, normally the largest single line on the schedule and the one that drives negative gearing. It is a deductible share rather than the full interest bill: "the interest on the loan must be apportioned into deductible and non-deductible parts according to the amounts borrowed for the rental property and for private purposes". Interest on loans taken out to buy depreciating assets, to make repairs and to fund renovations is claimed here too, so the amount is not tied only to the purchase mortgage.
value_definition: A dollar amount of interest only. Loan principal is not deductible and is not in this figure, and neither is the loan balance.
limitation: You cannot recover the debt or an interest rate from it, because the number is the owner's apportioned claim rather than the interest charged, and redraw and offset arrangements move that share around. A fall in the column across years can mean repayment, refinancing to private purposes, or a period when the property stopped being available for rent.
rationale: The guide devotes a section to this label, setting out when interest is deductible, that it must be apportioned where a loan has a private component, and which other borrowings can be claimed at the same line.
evidence_quote: the interest on the loan must be apportioned into deductible and non-deductible parts according to the amounts borrowed for the rental property and for private purposes
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label 'Interest On Loan(s)' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, leaving a reader free to read it as the property's actual interest bill or as a proxy for debt.

value_domain: ABS mesh block code, ASGS Edition 3 (2021)
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Mesh Blocks
variable_description: The finest geography available for the rental property, usually a block of about 30 to 60 dwellings. The ABS defines mesh blocks as "the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS" that "broadly identify land use such as residential, commercial, primary production and parks", and every other geography column on this row is built from it. It is the column to use when you want to characterise a property's immediate neighbourhood rather than its suburb.
value_definition: An 11-digit ABS mesh block code from the 368,286 mesh blocks of ASGS Edition 3, which cover Australia without gaps or overlaps and include 114 non-spatial special purpose codes.
limitation: The custodian's own label calls this the 2016 mesh block while the column name says 2021, so the edition has to be confirmed against the data before mesh blocks are joined to census or ERP files. A mesh block also carries a land-use category, not a count of people, so it cannot be read as the population near the property.
rationale: The column is an ABS mesh block code sitting with SA1 to SA4, LGA and state codes for the same address, and the ABS page gives the definition, the count and the special purpose codes.
evidence_quote: Mesh Blocks are the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS and form the building blocks for the larger regions of the Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Asgs 2016 meshblock' wording and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and never flagged that the label and the column name name different editions.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the other rental-related income line of the rental property schedule
value_source: ATO, myTax instructions 2025, Rent
variable_description: Money the property earned that is not rent: retained bond, insurance payouts and reimbursed expenses. The ATO names "any bond money you retained in place of rent or kept because of damage to the property requiring repairs", "an insurance payout for lost rent, or a reimbursement of any rental expenses" and "fees retained from cancelled booking". It adds to RNTL_INCM_AMT to give RNTL_GRS_AMT, so a large value against small rent usually marks a disrupted year rather than a high-yielding property.
value_definition: A dollar amount on an entitlement basis, taken up when the owner receives it or becomes entitled to it. Non-cash receipts are included at market value.
limitation: It cannot be read as extra profit, because the same events usually put a matching amount in the expense lines: a retained bond that funded repairs appears here and again as repairs and maintenance. It also gives no breakdown, so a bond, an insurance settlement and a cancellation fee are indistinguishable in the one number.
rationale: The myTax rent instructions name this exact field and itemise what belongs in it, and the rental properties guide sets the entitlement basis for the same amounts.
evidence_quote: any bond money you retained in place of rent or kept because of damage to the property requiring repairs
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label 'Other Rental Related Income' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could not tell whether it meant a second rent stream or one-off receipts.

value_domain: Percentage share of legal ownership in the rental property
value_source: ATO, myTax instructions 2025, Rent
variable_description: This taxpayer's share of the property as a percentage, and the number that reconciles the amounts on the row with what the owner may claim. The ATO instruction is simply "Enter the percentage amount of your ownership", followed by the warning that if you co-own the property "you need to be aware of the way that rental income and expenses are divided between co-owners", which is done by "dividing income and expenses according to legal interest". A jointly held property therefore appears once per owner, each row carrying the same ARID_HASH_TRUNC property key and a share that should total 100 per cent.
value_definition: A percentage from 0 to 100, held once per owner per property per income year, and applied by the lodgment software to derive that owner's share of every income and expense line.
limitation: It does not tell you whether the dollar figures beside it are the whole-property totals or the owner's share, and a lodger can override the calculated share, so the two need to be checked against each other before a per-property total is built. It also does not identify the co-owners, so partners in a couple cannot be paired from this column alone.
rationale: The myTax instructions define the field and state how the software uses it against the income and expense amounts, and the guide fixes the legal-interest rule the percentage is meant to record.
evidence_quote: If your ownership percentage is less than 100%, myTax will use your ownership percentage to calculate your share of the income amounts.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Ownership Percentage' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which left the crucial question of whose amounts sit on the row unanswered.

value_domain: Dollar amount claimed at the pest control line of the rental property schedule
value_source: ATO, Rental properties guide 2025, Rental expenses
variable_description: What the owner paid for pest treatment on this property and claimed immediately, rather than writing off over several years. Pest control is on the ATO's immediate-deduction list, subject to the rule that "You can claim a deduction for these expenses only if you actually incur them and they are not paid by the tenant". Amounts are small, so the column is more useful as a marker that the owner was actively maintaining the property than as a magnitude.
value_definition: A dollar amount deducted in the year it was incurred, apportioned where the property was available for rent for only part of the year or only part of it was rented.
limitation: Treatment done before the first tenancy is an initial repair and capital, so it should never reach this line, but the schedule cannot show whether a claim respected that. A zero is weak evidence of anything, since a strata property's pest treatment is usually inside the body corporate fee and a small job is often folded into sundry rental expenses.
rationale: The guide lists pest control among the expenses an owner can deduct immediately and states the incurred-and-not-paid-by-the-tenant condition that governs the whole block of expense lines.
evidence_quote: You can claim a deduction for these expenses only if you actually incur them and they are not paid by the tenant.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label 'Pest Control' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave no basis for judging what a zero or a small number means.

value_domain: Dollar amount claimed at the property agent fees or commission line of the rental property schedule
value_source: ATO, Rental properties guide 2025, Rental expenses, Property agent fees or commissions
variable_description: What the owner paid an agent to run the tenancy, which makes a non-zero value the clearest sign on the schedule that the property was professionally managed. The ATO describes it as "the cost of fees, such as regular management fees or commissions, you pay to a property agent or real estate agent for managing, inspecting or collecting rent for a rental property on your behalf". Selling commission and buyer's agent fees are excluded and go to the property's cost base instead.
value_definition: A dollar amount, deductible in the year incurred and claimable even for the period before the property was available to rent. It typically runs at a few per cent of gross rent, so it can be read against RNTL_GRS_AMT as an implied management rate.
limitation: A zero does not prove self-management: a fee bundled into a single agent statement can be reported at sundry rental expenses instead, and an owner who used an agent for part of the year leaves no trace of the switch. The line also cannot separate the ongoing management fee from letting and advertising charges the agent billed at the same time.
rationale: The guide has a section under this label naming what the fee covers and which agent costs are excluded, which is what decides whether the column can stand in for professional management.
evidence_quote: You can claim the cost of fees, such as regular management fees or commissions, you pay to a property agent or real estate agent for managing, inspecting or collecting rent for a rental property on your behalf.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label 'Property Agent Fees/Commission' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and never said that sale commissions are outside it.

value_domain: Count of weeks the property was rented in the income year
value_source: ATO, myTax instructions 2025, Rent, Rental property details
variable_description: How many weeks of the year this property actually had a paying tenant, which is what turns annual rent into an implied weekly rent. The ATO instruction is "Enter the number of weeks the property was rented out during the income year". Read with DT_PRPTY_FRST_RNTD on the same row it also separates a property let for the whole year from one that came onto the market partway through.
value_definition: A whole number of weeks, ordinarily 0 to 52, self-reported by the owner or their agent for the property as a whole rather than for the owner's share of it.
limitation: Weeks rented is not the deduction test. The ATO allows expenses for the period a property "was being rented or was genuinely available for rent", so a property advertised all year but tenanted for thirty weeks can still support close to a full year of claims, and a low count here does not imply the expenses were cut back. It also gives no vacancy pattern and no count of separate tenancies.
rationale: The myTax rent instructions name this field in the rental property details block and give the wording the lodger sees, and the rental expenses page supplies the availability test that the count is often mistaken for.
evidence_quote: Enter the number of weeks the property was rented out during the income year
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's sentence about the number of weeks and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never distinguished weeks rented from weeks available.

value_domain: Dollar amount at the gross rent line of the rental property schedule
value_source: ATO, Rental properties guide 2025, Worksheet - work out your net rental income or loss
variable_description: Everything the property brought in for the year before any deduction, and the top line of the schedule's arithmetic. On the ATO's own worksheet, gross rent is rental income plus other rental related income, and total expenses are then subtracted from it to give net rental income or loss. It is the natural denominator for yield and for expense ratios built from the other columns.
value_definition: A dollar amount that is the sum of RNTL_INCM_AMT and OTHR_RNTL_RLTD_INCM_AMT on the same row, measured on an entitlement basis rather than on cash received.
limitation: It is a derived subtotal of two columns already present, so adding all three across a portfolio double counts. It is also not the owner's cash receipts: rent owed but unpaid can be in it, and the amount may be the whole-property figure rather than this owner's share, which only OWNRSHP_PRCNT resolves.
rationale: The ATO worksheet sets out the schedule's structure line by line, showing gross rent as the sum of the two income lines and the base from which total expenses are subtracted.
evidence_quote: Net rental income or loss ($9,300 minus $20,629)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label 'Rent gross rent' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say that the column is a total of two others on the same row.

value_domain: Dollar amount at the rental income line of the rental property schedule
value_source: ATO, Rental properties guide 2025, Rental income
variable_description: Rent proper for this one property, separate from the bond and insurance receipts that sit in the other rental-related income column. The ATO defines the concept as "the full amount of rent and associated payments that you receive, or become entitled to, when you rent out your property", and payments in goods or services count at their market value. Divided by PRPTY_RNTD_WKS_THIS_YR_CNT it gives an implied weekly rent for the property.
value_definition: A dollar amount for a single property for a single income year, recognised when received or when the owner becomes entitled to it, and reported gross of the agent's commission rather than net of it.
limitation: Because the basis is entitlement rather than cash, rent that was billed and never paid can sit in the figure while the matching shortfall shows up later as retained bond or a legal claim. The amount also cannot be read as market rent, since a property let below market rates to a relative is reported at what was charged.
rationale: The guide's rental income section defines what rent and associated payments comprise and how non-cash rent is valued, which is what separates this line from the other rental-related income line beside it.
evidence_quote: Rental and other rental-related income is the full amount of rent and associated payments that you receive, or become entitled to, when you rent out your property.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label 'Rental Income' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not distinguish it from gross rent or from other rental-related income.

value_domain: Dollar amount at the net rent line of the rental property schedule, signed
value_source: ATO, myTax instructions 2025, Rent, and Rental properties guide 2025 worksheet
variable_description: The property's taxable result for the year: gross rent less total expenses, negative when the property is negatively geared. The ATO says "myTax will calculate Net rent based on the calculated amounts in Total gross rent and Total expenses", so it is arithmetic on the other columns rather than a separately reported figure. A negative value flows into the owner's taxable income and into the net rental property loss used in the income tests.
value_definition: A signed dollar amount equal to RNTL_GRS_AMT minus EXPNSS_TOTL_AMT on the same row, for one property and one income year.
limitation: It is not cash flow. Capital works deductions and decline in value reduce it without any money leaving the owner's account, while loan principal repayments consume cash and never appear, so a negatively geared property on paper can be cash positive and the reverse also happens. Being a subtotal, it must not be added to the income and expense columns.
rationale: The myTax instructions state how net rent is derived and the guide's worksheet shows the same subtraction line by line, which is what identifies the column as a computed total rather than an input.
evidence_quote: myTax will calculate Net rent based on the calculated amounts in Total gross rent and Total expenses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label 'Rent net rent' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it neither gave the formula nor warned that the figure is not cash flow.

value_domain: Dollar amount claimed at the repairs and maintenance line of the rental property schedule
value_source: ATO, Rental properties guide 2025, Rental expenses, Repairs and maintenance
variable_description: Work claimed immediately for restoring the property rather than improving it, which is the line most exposed to the repair-against-capital boundary. The ATO says "Repairs involve restoring a defective, damaged or deteriorated item to working condition" while "improvements, renovations, extensions and alterations" and "initial repairs" are capital and belong in capital works or the cost base. Read against CPTL_WRKS_DDCTNS_AMT on the same row, this column is the immediate half of the property's upkeep.
value_definition: A dollar amount deducted in the year incurred, covering both repairs and general maintenance such as repainting, and excluding any work an insurer paid for directly.
limitation: The column cannot tell a genuine repair from a capitalised improvement claimed as one, which is the most common error on the schedule, so it should be treated as a self-assessed claim rather than as measured maintenance spending. A spike also cannot be read as damage, since replacing a whole roof after a storm is a repair while replacing a whole stove is not.
rationale: The guide devotes a section and three worked examples to this label, drawing the repair-against-capital line that determines what may sit in the column.
evidence_quote: Repairs involve restoring a defective, damaged or deteriorated item to working condition and generally involve a replacement or renewal of a worn out or broken part.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label 'Repairs And Maintenance' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave no hint that the boundary with capital works is the whole difficulty of the column.

value_domain: ABS Statistical Area Level 1 code, ASGS Edition 3 (2021)
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Statistical Areas Level 1
variable_description: The rental property's neighbourhood at the level census data is normally released, about 400 people. The ABS says SA1s "are designed to maximise the geographic detail available for Census of Population and Housing data" and that they "generally have a population of 200 to 800 people". This is the level at which the property's location can be matched to census characteristics or to a socioeconomic index without disclosure problems.
value_definition: An 11-digit ABS SA1 code from the 61,845 SA1s of ASGS Edition 3, built from whole mesh blocks and aggregating to whole SA2s, including 34 non-spatial special purpose codes.
limitation: An SA1 describes the area, not the property, so attaching an area median income or an index score to a landlord's tenant is an ecological inference and not a measurement. Boundaries also change between ASGS editions, so a code cannot be joined to 2016 census output without a correspondence.
rationale: The column is an ABS SA1 code for the property's address, and the ABS page gives the design population, the count and the position of SA1s in the hierarchy above mesh blocks.
evidence_quote: SA1s generally have a population of 200 to 800 people, and an average population of about 400 people.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Statistical Area 1' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it neither gave the scale of the unit nor said the geography belongs to the property.

value_domain: ABS Statistical Area Level 2 code, ASGS Edition 3 (2021)
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Statistical Areas Level 2
variable_description: The suburb-scale area holding the rental property, and the smallest geography with published non-census statistics to join to. The ABS says SA2s "are generally the smallest areas used for the release of ABS non-Census of Population and Housing statistics, including Estimated Resident Population" and that they hold "between 3,000 and 25,000" people. For rental analysis it is usually the workable level, because SA2s are designed to represent communities that interact socially and economically.
value_definition: A 9-digit ABS SA2 code from the 2,473 SA2s of ASGS Edition 3, built from whole SA1s and aggregating to whole SA3s, including 19 non-spatial special purpose codes.
limitation: SA2s are not suburbs and their names are not gazetted locality names, so matching to a suburb-level rent series by name will silently mismatch. Populations range from a few thousand to twenty-five thousand, so an SA2 rate is far less stable in a remote area than in a city.
rationale: The column is an ABS SA2 code for the property's address, and the ABS page gives the population range, the count and the role of SA2s as the smallest non-census output unit.
evidence_quote: SA2s generally have a population between 3,000 and 25,000 with an average of about 10,000 people.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Statistical Area 2' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say what the unit is for or how it differs from a suburb.

value_domain: ABS Statistical Area Level 3 code, ASGS Edition 3 (2021)
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Statistical Areas Level 3
variable_description: The regional grouping the rental property falls in, of the order of a large council area or a cluster of suburbs. The ABS says SA3s "create a standard framework for the analysis of ABS data at the regional level through clustering groups of SA2s that have similar regional characteristics", with populations "between 30,000 and 130,000 people". It is the level to use when SA2 counts of rental properties are too thin to report.
value_definition: A 5-digit ABS SA3 code from the 359 SA3s of ASGS Edition 3, built from whole SA2s and aggregating to whole SA4s, including 19 non-spatial special purpose codes.
limitation: SA3s are built for regional comparability, not for administration, so an SA3 does not correspond to a council, a housing market or a planning region and cannot carry a policy boundary. Aggregating to this level also hides the within-region variation that makes rental markets differ street by street.
rationale: The column is an ABS SA3 code for the property's address, and the ABS page gives the design intent, the population range and the count.
evidence_quote: In general, SA3s are designed to have populations between 30,000 and 130,000 people.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Statistical Area 3' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it gave no sense of scale or of what the level is designed for.

value_domain: ABS Statistical Area Level 4 code, ASGS Edition 3 (2021)
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Statistical Areas Level 4
variable_description: The labour-market region the rental property sits in, the largest sub-state unit in the ASGS main structure. The ABS says "SA4 boundaries represent labour markets and the functional area of Australian capital cities" and are "designed with an emphasis on stability over time" so that series such as the Quarterly Labour Force publication can be published on them. That stability makes it the safest level for a long rental time series across ASGS editions.
value_definition: A 3-digit ABS SA4 code from the 108 SA4s of ASGS Edition 3, built from whole SA3s and aggregating to greater capital city areas and to states, including 19 non-spatial special purpose codes.
limitation: Most SA4s hold more than 100,000 people, so the level cannot distinguish an inner-city apartment market from an outer-suburban house market inside the same city. Its labour-market design also means the boundary answers where people work, which is not necessarily where a rental market clears.
rationale: The column is an ABS SA4 code for the property's address, and the ABS page gives the labour-market design, the stability intent and the count.
evidence_quote: SA4 boundaries represent labour markets and the functional area of Australian capital cities respectively.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Statistical Area 4' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the level is defined by labour markets.

value_domain: Dollar amount claimed at the sundry rental expenses line of the rental property schedule
value_source: ATO, Rental properties guide 2025, Rental expenses and net rental worksheet
variable_description: The residual expense line: deductible costs of the property that have no named line of their own. The ATO's immediate-deduction list has several such items - "bank charges", "secretarial and bookkeeping fees", "security patrol fees", "in-house audio and video service charges" and "servicing costs, for example, servicing a water heater" - none of which the schedule names. Its size relative to gross rent is a rough indicator of how much of the property's cost sits outside the standard categories.
value_definition: A dollar amount making up the last named row of the schedule's expense block, added with the other expense lines to give EXPNSS_TOTL_AMT.
limitation: What lands here is a preparer's choice rather than a category, so the column is not comparable between taxpayers and a named line can look artificially low simply because that agent pushed the cost into sundry. It also holds no code or description, so nothing inside it can be identified.
rationale: The guide's immediate-deduction list names deductible costs that have no line of their own on the worksheet, which is what the sundry line exists to hold, and the worksheet places it last in the expense block.
evidence_quote: secretarial and bookkeeping fees
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label 'Sundry Rental Expenses' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and never warned that the column's contents are not standardised.

value_domain: ABS state and territory code, ASGS Edition 3 (one digit)
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Australia and State/Territory
variable_description: The state or territory the rental property is in, which is what determines the land tax, stamp duty and tenancy law the property is subject to. The ABS says "States and Territories are identified by unique one-digit codes" and that Jervis Bay, Christmas Island, the Cocos (Keeling) Islands and Norfolk Island are "included as one geographic area at the State and Territory level under the category of Other Territories". It is the coarsest of the geography columns on the row and the one that survives every boundary revision.
value_definition: A one-digit ABS code covering the six states, the two internal territories and a combined Other Territories category, consistent with the leading digit of the SA1 to SA4 codes on the same row.
limitation: It locates the property, not the owner, so it cannot be used to say where the landlord lives or lodges from; an interstate investor's row carries the property's state. The ABS boundary is also cartographic rather than legal, so it should not be used to settle a jurisdictional question about a particular address.
rationale: The column is a one-digit ABS state code sitting above the SA4, SA3, SA2, SA1 and mesh block codes for the same property, and the ABS page gives the code structure and the Other Territories treatment.
evidence_quote: States and Territories are identified by unique one-digit codes as follows:
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'State or territory' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the code belongs to the property or that Other Territories is a single category.

value_domain: Dollar amount claimed at the stationery, telephone and postage line of the rental property schedule
value_source: ATO, Rental properties guide 2025, Rental expenses
variable_description: The small administrative costs of running the tenancy yourself: paper, postage and phone calls about the property. The ATO's immediate-deduction list carries "phone calls and rental" and "stationery and postage" as separate entries that this one schedule line combines. The amounts are trivial in dollars, so the column is read best as a flag that the owner did their own administration rather than as a cost.
value_definition: A dollar amount deducted in the year incurred, combining stationery, postage and the rental-related share of telephone costs for a single property.
limitation: The private and rental split of a phone bill is estimated by the taxpayer with no substantiation on the schedule, so the figure is among the softest on the row. It also cannot be compared with the agent fee column as a measure of effort, because an owner who uses an agent still incurs some of these costs and an owner who does not may never bother claiming them.
rationale: The guide's immediate-deduction list names phone calls and rental, and stationery and postage, which are the components this schedule line combines.
evidence_quote: stationery and postage
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label 'Stationery Telephone And Postage' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave no basis for judging the reliability of the number.

value_domain: PLIDA agency person identifier (anonymised)
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
variable_description: The landlord, not the tenant: the person key that ties this property schedule to the same taxpayer's income tax return. One person holding three rental properties has three rows for the year, all with this value and different ARID_HASH_TRUNC values, so the column is what turns a property file into a portfolio. ABS links across agencies through a "Person Linkage Spine" held "separate from the main body of data", so reaching a landlord's payments, health or census records means going out through the spine rather than joining on this identifier directly.
value_definition: An opaque identifier with no internal structure and nothing decodable in it. The same column name carries the person key on 41 of the synthetic PLIDA datasets, so it is the value you join on to reach the same person's tax, payment, health and census records; within a dataset it supports equality comparisons and nothing else.
limitation: It identifies the lodging owner, so a jointly held property produces two rows with two different values and the co-owners can only be paired by matching the property key ARID_HASH_TRUNC. The column also says nothing about anyone who lived in the property, and a landlord whose record failed to link to the spine is missing from every other PLIDA dataset rather than absent from them.
rationale: ABS documents the spine as the mechanism linking agency datasets and states that it is held apart from the data, which is why each agency file carries its own anonymised person identifier; the schedule's per-property structure explains why one person holds several rows in a year.
evidence_quote: The Person Linkage Spine allows us to link datasets through a spine of key information, separate from the main body of data.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's 'Synthetic id of individual person on dataset' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said that the person is the owner or that a person holds one row per property.

value_domain: Dollar amount claimed at the travel expenses line of the rental property schedule
value_source: ATO, Rental properties and travel expenses
variable_description: The cost of getting to the property to inspect it, maintain it or collect rent, including meals and accommodation on that trip. This is the one schedule line whose meaning changed by law partway through the series: "From 1 July 2017 you can't claim any deductions for the cost of travel you incur relating to your residential rental property" unless the owner is carrying on a business of letting rental properties or is an excluded entity. Values are therefore common up to 2016-17 and close to absent for residential property afterwards.
value_definition: A dollar amount for travel and associated meals and accommodation, apportioned where the trip also served another income-producing purpose or a private one.
limitation: A series built across the 2017 change is not continuous, and a drop after 2016-17 measures the law rather than owner behaviour. A non-zero value in a later year is also not necessarily an error, since commercial property and owners in the business of letting are still entitled to claim, and the schedule does not say which case applies.
rationale: The ATO page for this deduction gives the commencement date of the denial and the two exceptions, which is the fact that decides whether the column is comparable across years.
evidence_quote: From 1 July 2017 you can't claim any deductions for the cost of travel you incur relating to your residential rental property
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label 'Travel Expenses' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not mention that the deduction was withdrawn during the period the data covers.

value_domain: Dollar amount claimed at the water charges line of the rental property schedule
value_source: ATO, Rental properties guide 2025, Rental expenses
variable_description: Water charges the owner paid for the property and claimed, which in practice is the fixed service charge rather than the tenant's usage. The ATO excludes anything the tenant bears: you cannot claim for expenses "you don't incur, such as water or electricity usage charges borne by your tenants". Council rates sit in their own column, so this line is water and sewerage billing only.
value_definition: A dollar amount deducted in the year incurred, and claimable for the period the property was rented or genuinely available for rent, including during renovations undertaken with the intention of renting.
limitation: It measures who paid the bill, not how much water was used, so it cannot support any consumption or efficiency measure. A zero is ambiguous: it can mean the tenant is billed for usage under the lease, that the charge is inside a body corporate fee, or simply that the owner did not claim it.
rationale: The guide lists water charges among the immediate deductions and separately states that charges borne by tenants are not deductible, which is the split that determines what can be in the column.
evidence_quote: you don't incur, such as water or electricity usage charges borne by your tenants
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label 'Water Charges' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and never said that tenant-borne usage is excluded.
